videoIdeas.title: Nobody can string a sentence together anymore
videoIdeas.hook: You're not shy. You just never learned how to talk to people.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your own post on people struggling to string a sentence together (635 views) proves the appetite is there but the hook was buried in the caption. Dinoo is racking up 11k+ views on phone-addiction psychology framed as 'here's why you feel this way.' Turn your public speaking pillar into that same diagnostic format — the topic is on-brand and underexploited on your account.
videoIdeas.script: You're not shy. You just never learned how to talk to people, and your phone made sure you never had to. Back in the day you got dragged to the shop, you had to order the food, you had to talk to the uncle at the masjid whether you liked it or not. Now you can go a whole week without saying a full sentence out loud. So when you finally have to speak — an interview, a presentation, giving a khutbah reminder — your brain locks up and you call it anxiety. It's not anxiety. It's a skill you never practised. Speaking is a muscle. You don't fix it by reading about it, you fix it by being the one who orders at the counter, who asks the question in the lecture, who says salam first. Start small, start today, but start talking.

visuals.setting: Static talking-head, plain wall or car seat, natural light, casual — hoodie or plain tee. Calm, unbothered energy, like you're telling a younger brother a hard truth over lunch.
visuals.visualHook: Bold on-screen text 'IT'S NOT ANXIETY' while you sit silent for a half second before the first line lands.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open mid-sentence with no intro — just the line, jump-cut in
On-screen caption counting '0 sentences said out loud today' as a pattern interrupt
Hold up your phone to camera then set it down face-first before speaking

videoIdeas.title: 5 leadership habits the Prophet ﷺ had that nobody teaches
videoIdeas.hook: You keep chasing influence. The Prophetic model tells you to chase the opposite.
videoIdeas.rationale: Daanish's '5 careers I don't want' hit 155k and his '5 specialties' hit 28k — the numbered listicle is the highest-performing format in your niche right now. Your leadership pillar barely appears (one post, 508 views) despite being core to your brand. A Prophetic-leadership listicle marries the working format with your differentiator: Islamic framing done bluntly, not preachy.
videoIdeas.script: You keep chasing influence, followers, a platform. The Prophetic model tells you to chase the opposite. Five things. One — competence before clout. Al-Qawi wal-Ameen: strong AND trustworthy. Skill without integrity is just a dangerous man with a following. Two — he listened before he spoke. He'd let a man finish his whole complaint before saying a word. When did you last actually let someone finish? Three — he delegated. He didn't do everything himself, he built people who could. Four — he was consistent in private and public. Same man in the room as out of it. That's it, that's the whole game. Five — he served first. The leader ate last, carried bricks with everyone else. If your idea of leadership is being served, you've understood none of it. Save this and read the seerah properly.

visuals.setting: Talking-head, slightly more composed setting — bookshelf or clean neutral background, smart-casual. Steady, deliberate delivery, counting on fingers.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text '5 LEADERSHIP HABITS' with a subtle counter '1/5' ticking as you speak.
otherHookIdeas: Open on the number '5' large on screen then cut to your face
Pattern interrupt: 'chasing influence' text with a strike-through animation
End-card punchline text 'the leader ate last' held on screen for the loop

videoIdeas.title: Every uncle has an opinion on your degree
videoIdeas.hook: Every uncle and aunty has an opinion on your degree. None of them have read a green paper.
videoIdeas.rationale: This is almost verbatim one of your own captions (756 views) that never got developed into a proper hooked video. It's a genuinely sharp line that pattern-interrupts and speaks directly to young Muslims stuck between family expectations and their own path — pure mindset pillar. birdtart's 'strict parents / immigrant parents' angle pulled 64k, so the tension between family and career decisions is clearly landing right now.
videoIdeas.script: Every uncle and aunty has an opinion on your degree. None of them have read a green paper or a white paper in their life. Here's what nobody tells you: we have loads of people who can fix the thing — the doctors, the engineers, the coders. We have almost nobody who can decide whether the thing should exist at all. That's the gap. That's where the real leadership is, and it's empty because everyone got funnelled into 'safe' by people who confuse a job title with a life. I'm not telling you to drop medicine or law. I'm telling you the pressure you're feeling from the dinner table is not wisdom, it's habit. Respect them, but don't outsource your future to someone who's never had to make the decision you're making. Choose on purpose.

visuals.setting: Talking-head, kitchen or living-room setting to nod at the 'dinner table' theme, casual. Wry, knowing tone — a bit of a smirk on the uncle line.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'has an opinion' → 'has NOT read the paper' swap on the first line.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on you mid-eye-roll then straight into the line
Text punchline held at end: 'choose on purpose'
B-roll cut of a chai cup being poured to signal the family setting

videoIdeas.title: Stop refuting people online and go build something
videoIdeas.hook: I said I didn't want this to be a refutation page. Some of you don't help yourselves.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your commentary/refutation posts are your top performers (6k, 3k views) but they can trap you as a reaction account. This flips your own recurring theme into a leadership message: the gap between critics and builders. It keeps the blunt commentary energy your audience already rewards while pushing your leadership pillar and giving your feed a self-aware, higher-status angle competitors aren't touching.
videoIdeas.script: I said from the start I didn't want this to be a refutation page. And some of you genuinely don't help yourselves. But here's the wider point. It is so easy to be the critic. To sit behind a screen and pick apart everyone doing something. It costs you nothing. It builds nothing. Meanwhile the brothers opening cafés, running study circles, building third spaces — they're getting mocked by people who've never organised anything harder than a group chat. Understand this: the Ummah has never been short of critics. It's short of builders. Anyone can point at what's broken. Very few will put their name on fixing it. So before your next 'well actually' comment — ask what you've actually built this year. If the answer's nothing, close the app and go make something.

visuals.setting: Talking-head, direct to camera, plain background, slightly firmer energy — this one carries a bit more edge. Smart-casual.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'ANYONE CAN CRITICISE' as you open, mid-sentence with no soft intro.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on the blunt line 'some of you don't help yourselves'
Split-second flash of a comments section then cut to your face
Closing text card: 'the Ummah has enough critics'

videoIdeas.title: Read one boring book or stay average
videoIdeas.hook: You've read forty threads this week and not one book. That's the whole problem.
videoIdeas.rationale: birdtart's book content is exploding (331k on a reading video) and Daanish's journaling how-to hit 21k — 'input habits' content is peaking in the niche right now. You have zero of it. A blunt take on reading vs. doom-scrolling fits your mindset pillar and rides a proven format without copying anyone's exact angle.
videoIdeas.script: You've read forty threads this week and not one book. And then you wonder why your thinking feels shallow. Here's the uncomfortable bit — a thread is designed to be forgotten. It's junk food. It gives you the feeling of learning without any of the weight. A book makes you sit with an idea long enough to actually change. That's why it's harder, and that's exactly why it works. You don't need to read fifty books this year. Read one. A boring one. One that's slightly above your level and takes you a month. That single habit will put you ahead of almost everyone your age, because almost no one your age can sit with anything longer than fifteen seconds anymore. Pick the book today. Ten pages. That's the whole ask.

visuals.setting: Talking-head near a bookshelf or holding an actual book, warm lighting, relaxed. Conversational, honest — not preachy.
visuals.visualHook: Hold up a phone in one hand and a book in the other, then drop the phone out of frame.
otherHookIdeas: On-screen text '40 threads / 0 books' as the opener
Cold open flipping a book shut on camera
End text punchline: 'ten pages. that's the whole ask'

videoIdeas.title: Third spaces are the answer, so stop dunking on them
videoIdeas.hook: Young Muslims are finally building third spaces — and of course, some of you found a way to complain.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your third-spaces post (931 views) had a strong topic but a weak opening line buried under 'And rather than seeing...'. This is a timely community-leadership subject, and reframing it with a sharper hook can outperform the original. It sits squarely in your leadership pillar and taps the community-building conversation your audience clearly cares about.
videoIdeas.script: Young British Muslims are finally building third spaces — cafés, community hubs, study circles, actual places to belong. And of course, some of you found a way to complain about it. 'It's not Islamic enough.' 'They're just doing it for clout.' Listen. For years the complaint was there's nowhere to go, no space that isn't a masjid or a shisha lounge. Now people are building exactly that, with their own money and their own time, and the same crowd shows up to nitpick. This is what leadership actually looks like — it's unglamorous, it's someone signing a lease and hoping people turn up. You don't have to attend. But if you're not building, at the very least don't kneecap the ones who are. Support it, or get out of the way.

visuals.setting: Talking-head, ideally shot in or outside an actual café / community space if possible, casual, natural energy. If not, plain background works.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'FINALLY.' held for a beat, then straight into the line, filmed in a café setting.
otherHookIdeas: B-roll of a café interior then cut to you outside it
Pattern interrupt: 'of course some of you complained' as text
Closing card: 'support it or get out of the way'

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: This is your ceiling — 6,138 views, more than double anything else. The topic (protests in 2026) is urgent, emotionally charged, and the caption opens with a genuine hook: 'Can't believe we're still discussing the necessity of protests in 2026.' That disbelief framing pulls people in and the 15 comments show it divided opinion, which the algorithm rewards.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: The caption trails off mid-thought ('make themselves feel bett...') so the sharpest part of your point never lands in text. Front-load the full argument and cut the run-on so the payoff is readable at a glance. Also, this is pure commentary — pair the reach it earns with a call to actually do something so you're not just a reaction account.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: This is your public speaking pillar done right on subject — 'the amount of people who struggle to string a sentence together is shocking' is a strong, blunt observation that's core to your brand and differentiates you from the politics content.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 635 views and 0 comments is the tell: the idea was buried in a caption instead of being the spoken hook, and the framing was descriptive ('back in the days people would go outside') rather than confrontational. Open the video with 'You're not shy, you just never learned to talk to people' and ask a question that forces a comment. This topic can be a repeatable series, not a one-off.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 'Every uncle and aunty has an opinion on your degree. None of them have read a green or white paper' is your single best line in the whole set — it's specific, funny, and hits the exact family-vs-future tension young Muslims feel. 756 views on a non-political mindset topic proves the angle travels.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 4 comments for such a relatable jab means the video probably didn't drive people to react. End on a direct prompt ('tag the uncle') and make sure the fixer-vs-decider point lands in the first 15 seconds, not the caption. This is worth reshooting with the line as the literal opening frame.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: Refreshing self-awareness — 'I didn't want to make this account a refutation page but some people don't help themselves' shows personality and a clear stance, and 60 likes on 659 views is a strong like-to-view ratio, meaning the people who watched agreed hard.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: The reach is capped because refutation content mostly reaches people already in the argument. Convert this recurring frustration into a forward-looking leadership message (critics vs builders) so it pulls in people who aren't part of the beef. The caption also hedges ('may have some element of truth') — commit to the point faster.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: Great topic selection — third spaces is timely, community-focused, and squarely in your leadership lane. The caption lists concrete examples (cafés, hubs, study circles) which makes the point tangible rather than abstract.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 931 views but only 3 comments — the weakest engagement-per-view here. The caption opens as a neutral report ('Young British Muslims are creating third spaces') instead of taking a side, and the actual opinion is stranded after 'And rather than seeing...'. Lead with the tension ('people are finally building this and some of you found a way to complain') to spark the debate this topic deserves.
